rationale: ARC accelerates GPU atomic reductions in differentiable rendering by adding warp-level reduction and distributing atomic work between cores and L2 units, with both hardware and software implementations. It is a low-level GPU primitive/kernel optimization for a rendering workload.

POD-Attention is a GPU kernel that computes prefill and decode attention concurrently for hybrid LLM serving batches. It fuses two attention phases on the same SMs using software CTA scheduling to improve compute and memory-bandwidth utilization.

FlexAttention is a compiler-driven programming model that lowers user-defined attention modifications into fused attention kernel templates. It exists specifically to generate optimized kernels for many attention variants rather than hand-writing each fused kernel.

RASSM optimizes single-sparse-matrix kernels such as SpMM, SDDMM, SpMV, and SpTS using residue-guided adaptive tiling. This is directly a cache/locality and tiling optimization for sparse compute kernels on CPUs.

llm.npu is an on-device LLM inference system that chunks prompts, splits outliers to CPU/GPU, and schedules transformer blocks across CPU/GPU/NPU. These are graph/offload and heterogeneous scheduling policies above the kernel level rather than new kernels or kernel generators.

TileLink compiles tile-centric primitives into overlapped compute-communication kernels for distributed model execution. Fusing communication and computation kernels is explicitly within the kernel-style fusion family.

StreamGrid is a framework for designing streaming point-cloud accelerator architectures using line buffers, compulsory splitting, and deterministic termination. The evaluation is ASIC/accelerator design, so the contribution is hardware architecture and buffer sizing rather than software-realizable kernel optimization.

Cinnamon is a scale-out FHE framework for encrypted AI combining algorithms, compiler ideas, and hardware techniques for a proposed architecture. From the available abstract, the primary contribution appears to be FHE architecture/system scalability rather than a kernel or compiler for existing hardware kernels.

MAS-Attention schedules attention matrix and vector workloads across heterogeneous compute units with multi-tier tiling and cache-overwrite control on edge accelerators. This is a kernel/dataflow scheduling optimization for exact attention inference.

GPUlog implements Datalog as CUDA relational algebra kernels over the HISA data structure, with GPU-specific buffer management and join strategies. The contribution is a GPU kernel library/backend for Datalog execution.

HyC-LoRA is a LoRA fine-tuning method and memory-management system that compresses buffered activations with hybrid quantization/recomputation. The excerpts frame it as training memory compression integrated with ML frameworks, not as custom kernels or kernel-generation work.

QServe implements W4A8KV4 LLM serving with CUDA/PTX kernels, progressive quantization, register-level dequantization, compute-aware weight reordering, and KV4 attention. The low-bit format and supporting kernels are central contributions.
